new_entities.name: Low-dose colchicine after myocardial infarction
new_entities.description: Use of low-dose colchicine after recent myocardial infarction to reduce recurrent inflammatory cardiovascular events.

new_entities.name: Recurrent cardiovascular events
new_entities.description: Recurrent cardiovascular outcomes after an index myocardial infarction, including recurrent MI, stroke, angina requiring revascularization, or cardiovascular death.

edges.effect_quant: In COLCOT, low-dose colchicine lowered the post-MI primary composite endpoint from 7.1% to 5.5% (HR 0.77). ACS-focused meta-analysis pooling COLCOT-era trials found lower recurrent composite events (OR 0.67), though a broader 2025 post-MI meta-analysis reported a more mixed overall picture with no clear pooled reduction in adverse cardiovascular events.
edges.population: adults within days to weeks after acute myocardial infarction receiving contemporary secondary-prevention therapy
edges.mechanism: Colchicine suppresses inflammasome-driven neutrophilic and interleukin-1 mediated inflammation, which may reduce plaque instability and recurrent ischemic complications after infarction.
edges.summary: The strongest pro signal comes from COLCOT, and it is clinically meaningful enough to keep this edge positive overall. At the same time, the literature is no longer perfectly one-directional, so the confidence is lower than for classic lipid or blood-pressure interventions.
edges.caveats: Later syntheses have become more mixed, partly because event definitions and follow-up differ across trials and because gastrointestinal intolerance is common. This is a good example of a promising inflammatory strategy that is not yet as settled as LDL lowering.

evidence.citation: Bouabdallaoui N et al 2023 Cardiovasc Drugs Ther
evidence.notes: Colchicine in the Management of Acute Coronary Syndrome: A Meta-analysis.

effect_quant.comparator: recurrent composite cardiovascular events with colchicine versus placebo after acute coronary syndrome

evidence.citation: Tardif JC et al 2019 N Engl J Med
evidence.notes: Efficacy and Safety of Low-Dose Colchicine after Myocardial Infarction. COLCOT.

effect_quant.comparator: primary recurrent cardiovascular composite endpoint in COLCOT with colchicine versus placebo

evidence.citation: Shah S et al 2025 Clin Res Cardiol
evidence.notes: Efficacy and safety of colchicine post myocardial infarction: a systematic review, meta-analysis and meta-regression analysis of randomized clinical trials.

effect_quant.comparator: broader pooled post-MI adverse cardiovascular event risk was not significantly reduced with colchicine versus control in the 2025 meta-analysis
